name: co-tenants-day-180
bundle_path: <set to the implementation bundle for the run>
notes: Production's own organisation skew, as co-tenants for test cases 6 and 7. Shape from Q12: 986 organisations with 473 holding nothing, the largest holding 21% of all subjects. Sizes interpolated through the measured ranks rather than fitted, because no single power law holds across the range. The 473 empty organisations are not in this recipe -- they are rows rather than generated tenants, emitted by co_tenants.empty_rows(). bundle_path must be filled in before generating. **supervisor_level is per archetype, set 13 Oct 2026.** It was Sub-Centre, the TenantSpec default; on 6 Oct that was corrected to Taluka along with every other recipe, and that was wrong here for a reason the other recipes cannot show: the co-tenants are built from three *production* bundles, and only the customer's bundle has a Taluka. Generation raised on co-001 with "no level named 'Taluka'". Each archetype's chain, truncated at the deepest permitted registration type and uniform across every tenant of that archetype: large-pull-heavy is State > District > AWC Project Area > AWC Mandal > AWC Sector > AWC Village/Town > AWC Name, so supervision sits at AWC Village/Town; push-dominated is Block > Phc > Subcentre > Village, so Subcentre; media-heavy truncates to three levels, District > Block > Ward, its Village tier not being a permitted registration type, so its leaf is Ward and supervision sits at Block. One tier above the leaf in each case, which is what the scenarios mean by supervision one tier up. **Each tenant names a bundle_archetype rather than a bundle**, set 6 Oct 2026. The bundles are production exports whose filenames are organisation names, so a tracked recipe cannot name one; --bundle-root supplies a directory holding one extracted bundle per archetype and the mapping to organisations stays local. Assignment: the three ranks whose real bundles were obtained keep their own (1 large-pull-heavy, 3 push-dominated, 17 media-heavy) rather than being inferred. Ranks 2 and 4-20 go by measurement -- push share at or above 45% is push-dominated, otherwise files per pushed encounter above the platform's 0.2306 (MediaProfiles.MEASURED_BY_RANK) is media-heavy, otherwise large-pull-heavy. Ranks 21-513 are push-dominated: the model already treats everything past rank 20 as homogeneous (MediaProfiles.TAIL_RATE), and of the three it is the mid-sized config with a usable enrolment form -- the media-heavy bundle's only ProgramEnrolment mapping is voided, so tenants given it generate no enrolments and no programme encounters, which is right for two organisations and wrong for 490. That lands at 11 large-pull-heavy, 2 media-heavy, 500 push-dominated. **Organisation ids recorded 13 Oct 2026, after provisioning**, read back by name rather than derived: the recipe shipped with placeholders 1001-1513 and the server assigned 24-566. The ids are not contiguous -- 406-435 are missing, an id-allocation block the overnight restart discarded -- so a positional mapping would have been right for the first 382 tenants and wrong for the remaining 131, starting with co-383 at 406 against its actual 436. That is the failure the generator refuses to make on its own, and it loads cleanly. Matched on name from docs/co-tenant-provisioning.tsv, with co-001 (24) and co-002 (25) added: both pre-dated the run and the resume guard skipped them, so neither has a row in it.
